name: Charalambides
label: Kranky
lede: A Houston couple who met in a record store, named their band after one of its customers, stayed a band after the marriage ended, and spent three decades making slow, strange, beautiful noise mostly on cassettes and CD-Rs.

eras.title: A name off a customer list
eras.text: Tom Carter and Christina Carter met working at a Houston record shop and started a band that at first called itself Mutual Admiration Society. The early records came out on cassette with no label, then on Philadelphia's Siltbreeze.

years.h: Tom Carter, Christina Carter and Kyle Silfer start a band in Houston
years.p: The trio begins as Mutual Admiration Society. The band has always seen itself as mostly a duo of Tom and Christina Carter.

years.h: Charalambides: named after a record store customer
years.p: The band takes its name from the surname of a customer at the Houston record shop where Tom and Christina Carter met.

years.h: Our Bed Is Green · a 100-minute cassette with no label
years.p: Charalambides' first release is a C-100 tape the band puts out itself. Kranky reissues it as a double CD in 2005.
Tom Waters's Siltbreeze label, home of lo-fi noise and outsider rock, gives Charalambides its first vinyl.

years.h: Historic 6th Ward: a 90-minute tape that keeps coming back
years.p: Named for the old Houston neighborhood, the cassette is reissued on CD by the band's own Wholly Other label in 1996 and as a double LP by Time-Lag in 2002.

years.h: Market Square · a double LP for Siltbreeze
years.p: The band's second Siltbreeze record, and its first double album. The same year, Playtime issues the 7-inch Devils backed with Bid You Goodnight.

eras.title: Their own label, their own pace
eras.text: Charalambides started Wholly Other to release its own music, much of it on CD-Rs in editions of 100 to 250. The lineup at times included Heather Leigh Murray and Jason Bill, and the band joined the Six Organs of Admittance crowd later filed as New Weird America.

years.p: The band's third Siltbreeze release, and the last before Charalambides moves its albums to Kranky.

years.h: A split LP with Six Organs of Admittance
years.p: Charalambides' Second Rehearsal shares Songs From the Entopic Garden Volume 2 with Ben Chasny's Six Organs of Admittance, on Timelag. Eclipse also presses Branches Lathe in 100 copies.

years.h: IN CR EA SE and a pile of hand-numbered CD-Rs
years.p: Eclipse Records releases the double LP IN CR EA SE, alongside Wholly Other CD-Rs like CHT in 200 copies.

eras.title: The Kranky years
eras.text: Kranky gave Charalambides wide distribution for the first time. Five albums in five years, including a reissue of the first tape, are the records most listeners know.

years.h: Unknown Spin · a CD-R split, rescued by Kranky
years.p: The first Kranky album is the Charalambides half of a 2002 Wholly Other CD-R split with Scorces, Christina Carter's duo with Heather Leigh Murray.

years.h: Joy Shapes: Charalambides at full reach
years.p: The second Kranky album, released on LP and CD. Extra material from the 2003 sessions later comes out as Electricity Ghost on Wholly Other in 2007.

years.h: Kranky reissues Our Bed Is Green as a double CD
years.p: The 1993 cassette, the band's first release, gets a proper release twelve years on.

years.h: A Vintage Burden · on LP and CD for Kranky
years.p: The third Kranky album of new material.
The fourth Kranky album. The same year Wholly Other releases Strangle the Wretched Heavens, recorded 1994–96.

eras.title: Divorced, still a band
eras.text: Tom and Christina Carter divorced but kept Charalambides going as a duo, eventually from Austin. Their last Kranky album came in 2011, and in 2018 they put their own names on the cover.

years.p: Charalambides' fifth Kranky album of new music, on LP and CD.

years.h: Tom and Christina Carter, under their own names
years.p: The duo releases an LP and cassette titled Tom and Christina Carter on Drawing Room.
